subject.title: Feature: Telegram Reactions - Two-Way Support with Prompt Guidance

question: Should Telegram reaction prompt control remain part of existing `reactionLevel`, or should OpenClaw add the requested separate `reactionGuidance` config with explicit precedence, defaults, and notification gating?
rationale: The request adds a new public config surface that overlaps existing prompt-affecting `reactionLevel` behavior and adjacent reaction issues, so automation should not choose the product contract.

options.title: Unify Under reactionLevel
options.body: Keep one prompt-control source, add incoming soft-CTA guidance and notification gating through the existing reaction-level policy, and avoid a parallel config unless decoupling is proven necessary.

options.title: Add reactionGuidance
options.body: Implement the requested separate `off | minimal | full` option with documented precedence over or composition with `reactionLevel`, generated metadata, docs, and upgrade tests.

options.title: Defer Prompt Expansion
options.body: Keep current outgoing-only guidance and leave incoming reaction interpretation to the broader reaction feedback or wake-design effort.

recommendation.title: Unify Under reactionLevel
recommendation.body: Keep one prompt-control source, add incoming soft-CTA guidance and notification gating through the existing reaction-level policy, and avoid a parallel config unless decoupling is proven necessary.

likelyOwner.reason: This person has recent history in the reaction resolver, plugin prompt-routing path, and prior triage of this issue's config/prompt gaps.
